title: Isandro and the Landfall
premise: Ansel Eriksen, a riverboat captain haunted by a debt and a job she swore off years ago, is hired by her old rival Vess to run a forbidden monsoon-season passage upriver. The cargo turns out to be Isandro, a fugitive clerk carrying proof that Vess's shipping empire was built on drowned men's names — including the crew Ansel lost. Torn between loyalty to her old crew's memory and the truth Isandro carries, Ansel must survive the flood, Vess's hired gunboats, and her own guilt, choosing justice outside the law over the debt that has chained her. In the end, she scuttles her beloved boat to block Vess's escape channel, delivers the evidence to the river towns' council, and finds a new family aboard a patched-together steamer with Isandro at her side.
about_author: Xanthe Almeida spent a decade working seasonal freight on inland waterways before turning to fiction full-time. Her stories draw on river lore, monsoon country, and the quiet codes of people who live by the water.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Sandbar
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Introduces the riverboat Magpie, her skeleton crew, and the crushing debt owed to Vess's shipping line. A routine run shows Ansel's uncanny reading of the river and establishes what she lost years ago. Emotional beat: weary competence masking grief.

chapters.title: An Offer from Old Water
chapters.summary: Vess arrives at the dock with a contract: one monsoon-season passage to the upper reaches, triple pay, debt forgiven. Ansel refuses — that route was sworn off after the disaster — but Vess reveals the debt has been sold and called due in ten days. Emotional beat: dread tightening into a trap.

chapters.title: Cargo with a Pulse
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Forced to take the job, she discovers the sealed crate mid-river holds Isandro, a former records clerk fleeing Vess with a ledger of falsified manifests. Her crew demands he be put ashore; Ansel hesitates, recognizing his fear as her own from years past. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He shows Ansel the ledger: the 'lost' cargo runs were cover for scuttled boats and drowned crews, including the wreck that killed Ansel's old captain. Ansel burns dinner, says nothing, and stares at the river all night. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything she believed.

chapters.title: Gunboats at the Bend
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Vess's enforcement launch appears at a narrow bend, demanding Isandro be handed over. Ansel fakes engine trouble, hides him in the bilge, and talks her way through — but her first mate Tam suspects she's chosen a stranger over the crew's safety. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The storm hits early. The Magpie takes on water, the charts are useless against the flooded river, and only Ansel's instinct for the sandbars keeps them alive. Isandro works the pumps beside the crew and earns his first grudging nod from Tam. Emotional beat: strangers becoming shipmates.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Sweet Amity
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Storm-driven off course, they shelter in a dead slough — and find the rotting hull of the boat Ansel's captain died on, exactly where the ledger said it would be. Confronted with physical proof, Ansel finally admits the truth aloud. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Ten Days, One River
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. With the debt deadline days away, Tam confronts Ansel: finish the delivery, collect the pay, forget the ledger. Ansel instead proposes they turn back and bring the evidence to the river towns' council before Vess can silence it. Half the crew walks at the next landing. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing truth.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Climax. Vess's gunboats corner the crippled Magpie at the confluence. Outgunned, Ansel deliberately grounds and scuttles the Magpie across the channel's throat, stranding Vess's fleet while she and Isandro run the evidence overland through the flood to the council hall. Emotional beat: sacrifice made without hesitation.

chapters.title: A Boat Called Homecoming
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Resolution. Vess is arrested by the council's marshals; the debt dies with her contracts. The remaining crew pools their pay to buy a battered steamer, and Isandro — offered a pardon and a desk job — chooses the river instead. Ansel names the new boat. Emotional beat: found family anchored at last.
